title: AM Bench 2025 AMB2025-03: PBF-L Ti-6Al-4V rotating-bending HCF with pre-test XCT of gauge sections and killer-pore registration

chemistry.notes: Solid chemistry of specimen 800HIP-106 after heat treatment; 800VAC-85: Al 6.30, V 3.76, O 0.10, C 0.01, N 0.02, H 0.003, Fe 0.17. Both meet ASTM F3001.

processing.parameters: 3D Systems DMP Flex 350 (software 36.15.13); 245 W laser power, 1250 mm/s scan speed, 60 um layer, 80 um beam spot, 245 deg scan rotation between layers, no baseplate preheat, 99.999% Ar. Plasma-atomized powder 10-45 um (D10 21, D50 35, D90 47 um). All fatigue specimens built vertically.
processing.heat_treatment: Two conditions from one build: 800HIP = 800 C, 2 h, 200 MPa Ar, ~12 C/min cooling; 800VAC = same thermal cycle in vacuum furnace with ~75 mTorr Ar partial pressure (no pressure; porosity not closed).
processing.surface_condition: Machined and polished per ISO 1143 (Ra <= 0.2 um; measured avg Ra ~0.09-0.13 um)

acquisition.facility: Lab Zeiss Xradia Versa XRM-500 (NIST)
acquisition.volume_dimensions: Entire RBF gauge section from 4 stitched FOVs; typically >3200 slices of ~1004 x 1024 pixels
acquisition.notes: 140 kV, 71 uA, 4.0 s exposure, 1601 projections/360 deg, HE2 filter, 16-bit, beam hardening factor 0.25; reconstructed with Zeiss Scout-and-Scan 14.0.1. XCT on five RBF specimens prior to fatigue. Pores segmented with IMPPY3D (non-local-means denoise, hysteresis threshold, convex-hull closure for near-surface features). Lead-particle fiducial used to register fracture-origin (killer) pore to XCT.

microstructure.grain_size_um: alpha lath mean area ~25.06 um^2 (800VAC) and ~24.13 um^2 (800HIP) from EBSD (2D)
microstructure.texture: EBSD texture provided in calibration data

defects.statistics: Per-specimen CSVs of labelled pores (centroid, volume, equivalent spherical diameter, sphericity, rotated bounding box extents), porosity of scanned region, cross-sectional area vs gauge length; sqrt(area) measurements of killer defects provided in answers data. 800HIP sealed internal porosity.

mechanical_properties.other: 800HIP avg (n=3): YS 1004.8 MPa, UTS 1089.5 MPa, E 153 GPa, uniform el. 5.2%, total el. 19.4%. 800VAC avg: YS 999.6, UTS 1082.6, E 150 GPa, uniform 6.2%, total 15.6%. ASTM E8, strain rate 0.001/s. No statistically significant differences.

fatigue.loading: Four-point rotating bending (ISO 1143), R = -1, 100 Hz, ADMET eXpert 9313; ~24-25 specimens per condition
fatigue.results: Full S-N data for 800HIP (calibration) and both conditions (answers_data/fatigue_both_conditions.xlsx). Challenge asked for 800VAC S-N, specimen-specific fatigue strength and failure location.
fatigue.crack_initiation: 800VAC specimens initiated at internal/near-surface pores; killer pores identified on fracture surfaces by SEM/optical fractography and registered to labelled XCT pore IDs (xct_fractography_registration). HIP specimens showed surface-based initiation (SEM confirmation).

data_availability.format: Zeiss .xrm/.txrm radiographs, 16-bit/8-bit TIFF stacks, segmented and labelled stacks, VTK, CSV, XLSX, EBSD data

references.citation: NIST AM Bench, AMB2025-03 Measurements and Challenge Problems description (2025)
Benzing J., Moser N., Derimow N., Kafka O., Saville A., et al., AMB2025-03 High-Cycle Rotating Bending Fatigue Tests of PBF-L Ti-6Al-4V (dataset), NIST

title: L-PBF IN718 as-built surfaces with 0/1/2 contour passes: XCT surface/porosity + rotating-beam HCF (NIST)

processing.parameters: Vertical specimens; only the number of contour passes varied (0, 1, 2) to give three as-built roughness levels; compared with polished specimens. Build CAD files and HIP cycle log provided in dataset. Data folders labelled '30um' (likely layer thickness; unverified).
processing.heat_treatment: HIP cycle documented in dataset (build_data/heat_treatment/HIP_cycles NIST In718 11292021.xlsx); details not extracted

acquisition.facility: Lab XCT (NIST); instrument not verified
acquisition.volume_dimensions: Full 16-bit TIFF stacks per specimen (e.g. ~5.8 GB zipped for specimen 1p1)
acquisition.notes: 3D images, binary segmentations, scan settings files, and imppy3d Python scripts for segmentation, internal porosity and surface-roughness/notch extraction for 6 specimens of particular interest.

defects.statistics: Per-specimen surface-profile CSVs (0.46-0.78 GB each) and deepest-surface-notch (sv3d) tables. Roughness increased as contour passes decreased.

title: As-built L-PBF IN718 process-structure-property set: 25 parameter sets HCF, micro-CT pore structure, tensile, VDF fracture prediction

chemistry.notes: 3D Systems IN718 powder (recycled within vendor standards); composition not extracted.

processing.parameters: 3D Systems ProX DMP 320. 25 parameter sets: laser power 115-465 W (11 values), scan speed 620-1770 mm/s (13 values), layer thickness 30 or 60 um, build orientation 0/60/90 deg; hatch 100 um, spot 50 um; energy density ~30-90 J/mm3. Contours 115 W/625 mm/s (30 um) or 165 W/625 mm/s (60 um). 3 fatigue specimens per set (75 total), ASTM E466 flat specimens (6.36 x 3.10 mm gauge).
processing.surface_condition: As-built surfaces for HCF; some machined specimens for tensile/meso tests

acquisition.facility: Lab Zeiss Xradia Versa 520 (Paper 2) and Zeiss Xradia Versa 500 (Paper 3, pre/post deformation)
acquisition.notes: Paper 2: 160 kV, 10 W, 1 um voxel. Paper 3: 130-160 kV, 10 W, ~2 um voxel (some 1 um 'vertical stitch' scans downsampled); XCT before and after tensile deformation of 6 meso-scale specimens (per Watring dissertation, Univ. Utah 2021).

microstructure.phases: gamma matrix with Nb/Mo-rich secondary precipitates (as-built)

defects.statistics: Porosity (micro-CT): ~6.91% for 0 deg/38 J/mm3; 0.23% for 0 deg/62 J/mm3; 0.07% for 60 deg/62 J/mm3 (Watring dissertation). Paper 3 meso specimens 0.01-0.08% porosity.

mechanical_properties.other: Condition 0 deg/62 J/mm3: YS 798, UTS 1081 MPa, E 195 GPa, uniform el. 22%, total el. 29%. 60 deg/62 J/mm3: YS 772, UTS 1070, E 194, total el. 28%. 0 deg/38 J/mm3: YS 639, UTS 774, total el. 6%.

fatigue.loading: Axial tension-tension, sigma_max 600 MPa, R = 0.1, 20 Hz, MTS 810, as-built surfaces
fatigue.results: Bell-shaped life vs energy density for fixed orientation; max life at 60 deg / 62.15 J/mm3 / 30 um layer. Life decreased with surface roughness.
fatigue.crack_initiation: Surface-crack initiation sites increased with roughness (build orientation); low energy density -> lack-of-fusion pores, high energy density -> spherical (possibly keyhole) pores. Initiation identified by SEM fractography, not tracked in CT for HCF specimens; CT used for pore networks and VDF-based fracture-location prediction in tension (4/6 correct).

title: PBF-L Ti-6Al-4V with 15 novel HIP/heat treatments: XCT porosity (8.5 and 1.25 um), 300 mini-tensile tests, RBF S-N (NIST)

chemistry.notes: Builds conformed to ASTM F3001; measured oxygen 0.104 wt% (NIST IR 8551). Full chemistry in dataset.

processing.parameters: 3D Systems DMP Flex 350; 245 W, 1250 mm/s, 60 um layer, Ar at 150 mbar, O2 < 10 ppm; powder 10-45 um (D50 30-36 um). 94 blocks (tensile) + cylinders for RBF.
processing.heat_treatment: 15 conditions HT0 (as-built) to HT14: stress relief, new/classic sub-beta HIP, super-beta HIP, with furnace/fast/rapid-quench cooling, ageing and tempering steps (e.g., HT4 nsHIP+FC, HT10 csHIP+FC, HT14 SHIP+RQ+T3+FC). 800 C HIP steps at 200 MPa.
processing.surface_condition: RBF specimens machined and longitudinally polished (240/320/600 grit)

acquisition.facility: Lab North Star X50 (8.5 um voxel; 160 kV, 55 uA, ~3200 projections) and Zeiss Xradia Versa XRM-500 (1.2525 um voxel; 160 kV, 62 uA, ~1000 projections)
acquisition.volume_dimensions: Blocks for all 15 HTs at 8.5 um; sub-volumes of HT0/1/2/3/13 at 1.2525 um
acquisition.notes: 16-bit TIFF stacks exported; analyzed with NIST open-source Python (imppy3d).

microstructure.phases: alpha' (as-built) to alpha+beta with varying morphology; Ti3Al (alpha2) precipitation after ageing (Derimow et al. 2025)

defects.statistics: XCT porosity (vol%): HT0 as-built 0.00089 (8.5 um) / 0.00130 (1.25 um); HT1 SR 0.00238 / 0.00760; all HIP conditions 0.00000 at both resolutions.

mechanical_properties.other: 300 mini-tensile tests (15 conditions x 2 orientations). Avg YS (both orientations): HT4 982 MPa, HT10 883 MPa, HT14 823 MPa.

fatigue.loading: Four-point rotating bending, R = -1, 6000 rpm (100 Hz), ADMET eXpert 9300, runout 1e7 cycles
fatigue.results: Runout stress (N=3 runouts): HT4 662 MPa (67% YS), HT10 637 MPa (72% YS), HT14 462 MPa (56% YS). S-N data in S-N_data.xlsx.
fatigue.crack_initiation: Porosity closed by HIP, so fatigue isolates microstructure; RBF fractography images provided. Initiation not linked to CT defects.

title: SLM AlSi10Mg three process generations: CT defect populations, killer-defect sqrt(area), defect-tolerant S-N prediction

processing.parameters: EOS M400, 2015-2017; processes P1, P2 (same params, improved gas recirculation) and P3 (layer 60->30 um, platform preheat 200->165 C). Vertical and horizontal specimens.
processing.surface_condition: Machined, Ra 0.33 um, Rz 2.99 um (ASTM E606 geometry, gauge vol 201-452 mm^3)

acquisition.facility: Lab GE Phoenix v|tome|x m at ESA ESTEC; VG Studio Max 2.2.1 analysis

microstructure.grain_size_um: Melt pools 60-140 um deep, 70-230 um wide

defects.statistics: Defect density (def/mm^3): P1 10.8, P2 23.8, P3 1.9; density >100 um: P1 0.64, P2 0.20, P3 4.5e-3. Largest defects elongated (LOF). Al2O3 inclusions in P2. Gumbel/LEVD estimates of killer size.

mechanical_properties.other: P3 horizontal: E 70.2 GPa, Rp0.2 291.0, Rm 443.7 MPa, A 6.6%. P1 horizontal: Rp0.2 224.9, Rm 365.3. P2 horizontal: 304.5 / 441.5.

fatigue.loading: Axial force control, R = -1 (minus sign lost in text extraction; consistent with context), 30 Hz (ESTEC, Instron E10000) and 15 Hz (PoliMi, MTS 810); P1 18, P2 45, P3 42 HCF tests; some specimens with artificial micronotches at 97.5% percentile of max defect
fatigue.results: Life improved P1 -> P2 -> P3 with decreasing max defect size; vertical lower than horizontal (5-28%).
fatigue.crack_initiation: Failures from killer defects (mostly LOF) measured as sqrt(area) on SEM fractography; CT-based extreme-value estimates of killer size bracket observed values.
